entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

I spelled out what it means: version 1, every migration path removed (not just the new 3→4 step), and any file with a different version loads as a fresh, empty document. That last part means project-state files you saved during development will lose their chats. I also told it not to start the live batch until you approve one. Its native build finished cleanly at 17:23. Its tests haven't run yet.

## Plan for the live batch

**First, at no cost.** Run the native and shell-harness tests, then re-record `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` with the scripted model. Those recordings still contain the removed `origin` field.

**Batch A: the standard project-prompt evaluation. 75 runs.**
- All 25 cases, 3 runs each, on DeepSeek V4 Flash with the pinned host. I run only the new prompt and compare it case by case with the October 19 baseline, as you asked earlier today.
- Why it's needed: the change alters three things the model reads in every conversation. The `plan_set` description is new, the `origin` field is gone, and the plan now stays "current" after the agent's own edits.
- Cost: the October 19 baseline used about 1.2M input tokens for the same 75 runs, about 0.9M of them cached. I expect about the same.

**Batch B: headline journeys in the real app. 12 runs.**
- 4 cases, 3 runs each: a strength print, an appearance print that needs supports, a quick fit-check prototype, and a changed strategy. In the last one, a second message changes the goal and the headline should change with it.
- Each run loads one model into a clean project and lets the live agent work with real tools. This is not the canned-reply setup that wasted tokens on October 10. The harness's limit is 40 tool calls per turn; I'd lower it to 20.
- For every run I'd report:
  - the exact headline and its word count;
  - whether the agent called `plan_set` at all;
  - in the changed-strategy case, whether the headline was rewritten or stayed stale;
  - what the card showed at the end.
- No pass/fail thresholds: I read each run and tell you what looks wrong. Three runs per case won't give a reliable rate. They will show whether headlines are usually missing or generic, which was the October 12 problem.
- Cost is a guess, because no real-app journey has been measured: about 500k input tokens per run (roughly 20 requests at about 25k each, mostly cached), so about 6M for all 12.
- To limit that risk, I'd run one journey first, report its actual token use, and only run the other 11 if it's within twice the estimate. If it costs more, I come back to you.

**Total:** 87 runs, about 7M input tokens estimated. I'd log usage from every response and report the actual total.

entries.name: mcp__ccd_session__start_session
entries.description:
Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so); the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. content.text:
The setup-card headline work is committed as f964221268 on branch `claude/setup-card-headline` (not pushed), and the approved live batch is done. I checked the branch myself: the commit is there, the working tree is clean, the schema version is 1, and no migration code is left. The [implementation session](#local_cbad1a66-0d1c-4d7c-848b-8ec06545874b) reports that all tests pass (338 native agent-bridge cases, 444 page tests, and the shell-harness and real-adapter harness runs). I didn't rerun them.

**What changed:**
- The setup card shows the plan headline where the preset differences used to be.
- Each chat stores its own intent and plan. A new chat starts with no plan.
- The in-app agent's own edits no longer mark its plan as stale.
- The `origin` field and the code that tracked which settings the agent wrote are gone.
- "N objects with overrides" stays on its own line.
- The schema reset affects your files: project-state files saved during development will load as empty documents and lose their chats.

**The live batch: 12 journeys on DeepSeek V4 Flash, 4.5M input tokens (3.7M cached) and 91k output.**
- All 12 runs called `plan_set` and produced a headline of 7 to 12 words.
- In all three changed-strategy runs the headline was rewritten after the goal changed. For example, "Spiral vase mode for a lightweight, single-wall dried-flower vase" became "Multi-wall vase with infill for watertight strength, PLA on X1 Carbon."
- That's a clear improvement over October 12, when one journey never called `plan_set` and the other two were generic.

**What still looks wrong:**
- **Headlines still mention things the prompt says to leave out.** Five name the object ("PETG wall hook", "Rhino figurine"), one repeats the purpose ("for 5 kg load"), one names the printer, and one ends on routine preparation ("proper bed choice"). The extra words make headlines longer, but none is misleading.
- **The purpose title went stale in two changed-strategy runs.** The model rewrote the headline but never updated the purpose, so the card read "spiral vase for dried flowers" above a multi-wall watertight strategy. This prompt problem existed before this branch. I've proposed it as a separate follow-up (the card above).
- **A headline can arrive before its settings.** In one run, the new headline showed above the old spiral-vase estimates. The handoff accepted this, since a headline states intent, not applied settings.
- **Pictures were removed from every request.** The pinned model hosts reject images, so the model never saw the plate pictures. The batch says nothing about behavior that depends on them.

Not tested end to end: that the card's own Undo button counts as your edit. The code and a fake-workspace test say it does, but it wasn't exercised through the real button.

=== 28d6d67fdc
Merge intent_update and plan_set into one tool, setup_record

In batch B's changed-strategy runs the model rewrote the plan headline with
plan_set but never called intent_update, so the setup card's title still
named the old goal above the new strategy. The two records make up the card
and were already handled as one (same coordinator block, both in-app only,
both on the chat, the same context push), so they become one tool.

setup_record takes:
- setupTitle, required on every call: what the person wants, in their words.
  Restating it with each plan keeps title and headline from drifting apart.
  A title the chat refuses (more than one line or 120 characters) records
  nothing, the plan included.
- fields, optional, with intent_update's semantics (assumed, question,
  provenance).
- plan, optional: headline, decisions, assumptions, risks. Given, it
  replaces the whole plan; left out, the plan is kept. A purpose can be
  recorded before a strategy exists: a title-only call, the setup check,
  then a later call with the plan.
The result carries the intent section, purposeChange and the setup in force
as intent_update's did, and always the plan as it now stands. The
description keeps the concise-headline wording and states the split: the
title is what the person wants, the headline is how the agent will print.

The setup-changed skill fires on a setup_record whose purposeChange is
first or changed (a first purpose or changed fields), as before; a new
title alone is title_only, and a call that only restates the purpose to
change the plan is unchanged, so neither fires it. The card's context is
pushed once per successful call, so title and headline arrive together.

Changes to the model's input: one tool where there were two (27 project
tools, not 28), the project prompt's "recorded with setup_record", and the
setup-changed skill's "record the plan and its assumptions with
setup_record first". tests/project_prompt: grading, script, README,
project_tools.json and requests.json updated and re-recorded with the
scripted model; no live calls.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M5BMQDRNV2BHT3S97D58ZP7P

=== f964221268
Store intent and plan on each chat; show the plan headline on the setup card

Each chat now owns its print intent, purpose setup and plan. The project's
current ones are the active chat's, read through activeConversationId and
stored nowhere else. A new chat, and the replacement made when the active
chat is deleted, starts with a copy of the active chat's intent and no plan.
Resuming a chat makes it active and restores its model version; its intent
and plan never left it. A chat checkpoint keeps only the model version, the
boundary, the time and the card summary; the saved card reads its title and
headline from its own chat.

Region annotations belong with the model. Saved model versions held no
project-document state at all (restore always kept the current document, so
the old header comment about taking the earlier version's intent and plan was
wrong). Each version manifest now records the document's region list when it
is saved, a change to that list counts as a new version, and restoring or
resuming a version puts its list back.

The project-state schema is reset to version 1 with no migration, because
the project is not live yet: a document of any other version loads as a
fresh one, like a corrupt one. The older-record reads go with it (activity
source guessed from the correlation id, numbered default titles, the
skeleton merge and viewed-chat backfill), as do the version store's
first-format HEAD, the version-1 current-state wrapper and per-version
state.json reads. Project-state files saved during development load as fresh
documents and lose their chats.

The setup card shows the plan's headline in place of the preset-difference
rows, in every card state, and no line when there is no plan. The
"N objects with overrides" note stays on its own line. plan_set pushes the
card's context when it succeeds. The detailed setup page keeps every
difference, in OrcaSlicer's own preset/page/group order. Removed: the card's
difference selection, ranking, "more changes" count and "No changes from
presets" line, and the agent-authorship layer (remembering patch results,
replaying activities, binding to presets, the two maps).

Two intentional changes to the model's input, both in the re-recorded
tests/project_prompt/requests.json:
- preset differences no longer carry "origin";
- the in-app agent's own edits no longer mark its plan needs_reassessment.
  A person's edit (Undo and Redo included), an external MCP client's edit
  and a version restore still do. The recording's 240 needs_reassessment
  values are now current.
A third: a new chat's model sees no plan until it calls plan_set; before,
it inherited the previous chat's. plan_set's description now asks for a
short strategy headline (about 8 to 12 words) and a refresh when the
strategy changes.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M5BEAGNDKC4S0C90G4QA26CE

2026-10-20T04:14:23.692Z | Mostly yes, I think it's how we prompted it, and it isn't new with the merged tool. That's a hypothesis from the transcripts, not something I've tested.

**The evidence: the old tool did the same.** Batch B still used `intent_update`, whose description said only "Record the user's explicit purpose as setupTitle". Seven of its twelve titles already carried settings or strategy:

- "PETG wall hook for 5 kg backpack - 6 walls, 25% infill"
- "Wall hook for 5 kg backpack - PETG HF, Strength profile, Textured PEI Plate"
- "Rhino figurine — 0.16mm, 3 walls, organic supports"
- "Display vase for dried flowers — Spiral Vase mode, PLA, X1C"

So the merge didn't cause this. It made it more visible, because title and headline now come from the same call and you can see them repeat each other.

**Why I think the prompting invites it:**

1. **The field's name says "setup", not "purpose".** It's called `setupTitle`, so a model reads it as "a title for the setup" and describes the setup. Field names tend to weigh more than the sentence explaining them.
2. **The title gets no limits; the headline gets several.** For the headline I wrote what to leave out (the purpose, the file name, the printer, routine steps) and a word target. For the title there's nothing like "no settings, material or printer". In practice the only rule it has is the 120-character limit.
3. **The model doesn't know what else the card shows.** Nothing tells it the presets line and the headline sit right under the title. So it packs everything into the title to make it stand on its own.
4. **The surrounding wording points the same way.** The project prompt says "a setup that suits the print's purpose, recorded with setup_record", which reads as "record the setup". And the `fields` show the same habit: the model filled them with "Printer=Bambu Lab X1 Carbon" and "Material=PLA", copying configuration rather than what the person said.

A cheaper, less capable model like DeepSeek V4 Flash probably follows names over prose more than a stronger one would. But all four points are in our wording, so that's where I'd fix it first.

**What I'd change:**
- Rename `setupTitle` to `purpose`.
- Describe it as the person's goal in a few words, in their terms, with no settings, material or printer unless the person made those the goal. Add one good and one bad example.
- Lower its limit to about 60 characters.
- Say in one line that the card shows the presets and the headline under it.
- Reword the project prompt line to "the print's purpose, recorded with setup_record". It's a small code change plus a re-recording, with no live calls.

To check the fix, the cheapest test is the standard project-prompt evaluation. Its `prepare-petg-strong` case grades exactly this first call, so I'd add a check that the title contains no settings. Any live run still needs Kenneth's approval of a specific batch.

Do you want me to make the change on this branch?

It loads one model into a clean project with the live Agent, writes `turn-N.json` (conversation, every tool call with arguments and result, pictures as `.b64`) once the chat has been quiet for 8 s, then waits for `next-N.txt` holding the next user message or `END`. The run script and viewer were `run_probe.sh` and `show_turn.py` in that session's scratchpad; the key comes from `JusPrin2.conf` through `OPENAI_API_KEY`, with a scratch `$HOME` per run.

Measured cost on gpt-5.4-mini: 3 conversations (file-load message plus 2 user turns each) were 31 requests and 267,803 tokens, 82% of the input cached. Real tool results, no canned replies, so it fits [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]].

Thingiverse: `curl` on `https://www.thingiverse.com/download:<id>` gets a 403 bot check. Open `thing:<id>/files` in the built-in browser, `find` the "Download <name>" button and click it; the file lands in `~/Downloads`.

Result of that session's test (current core prompt, 55a2d37618): in 3 of 3 conversations the assistant never called `view_render`, never said what the model was, and sliced with stock settings; see [[project-prompt-eval-sample-size]] for why 3 runs is an observation, not a rate.

Some product state is not held anywhere in OrcaSlicer: the print intent, the pinned agent plan, semantic region annotations, physical facts the user confirmed about a printer, and the monitoring rules the user sets for automatic pausing. For this state, the "current Orca owner" step in the route above is a JusPrin store instead. Every other step stays the same. The rules are:

State that belongs to a printer (confirmed facts, monitoring policy) stays in app data, stored per printer identity, the way `PrinterFactsStore` keeps it. Confirmed facts carry an expiry, because the physical world changes without telling the app. See [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md).

- **Revision.** Every write has to signal that it happened, so that readers read again. Two questions are still **open**: which signal to use, and whether the signal invalidates actions that are already queued. They belong to the milestone that adds the first writer. The obvious answer would be to publish a `WorkspaceChangeReasons` bit and add that bit to `kInvalidatingReasons`. That cannot be built as described. `settings_apply_patch` requires its caller's `expectedRevision` to equal the current revision exactly. So if the revision goes up at any point between a client's preview and its apply, the apply fails as `stale_workspace`. An agent that recorded its plan between previewing and applying would make its own call fail. There is an existing example of the alternative: the edit feed (`WorkspaceEditHub`) reports a change without raising the revision. Decide separately for each kind of state. A region annotation generates OrcaSlicer artifacts, so it is a real change to the project. An answer about intent, or a statement of the plan, is not. In the code as built, writing a region record signals nothing by itself. The artifacts it generates are ordinary OrcaSlicer edits, and they raise the revision in the usual way. So an action that was queued before an annotation goes stale, exactly as it would after any other edit to the model.

lines: A skill is a file on the Agent page, `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: frontmatter with its `name` and a `trigger`, a `description` or both, then the text the model gets. The page sends every skill once per connection with the `skills` bridge message. A skill with a trigger is the app's: when the event it names happens, the host adds it to the one request where the model first reads about the event, as the request's last item, and to no later request. A skill with a description is the model's: `skill_read` lists the described skills in its own description and returns one by name, and is offered only while at least one exists (none does yet). Four skills have triggers, one file each:

- `file-loaded` (trigger `file_loaded`): the first message after a file is opened or imported is a judgement about the load report. It fires when the person opens or drops a file, after an in-app `object_import` (and a failed `project_open`) in the same turn, and in the opened project's chat after an in-app `project_open`, which replaces the conversation and so ends the turn that asked. An MCP client's loads fire nothing. The host sends a picture of the active plate with it and, when no purpose is recorded, one sentence of its own built from that state.

-- `project-setup-changed` (trigger `setup_changed`): check the setup in force against the print's purpose. It fires on the result of an in-app `intent_update` that recorded a purpose for the first time or changed it (its result says which in `purposeChange`), when the printer, filament, process or plate type differs from the setup the model was last asked to check under a recorded purpose (on the next tool result of the turn, or on the next turn's first request when the person changed it by hand), and on a turn's first request after the person restored an earlier version while a purpose is recorded. Each time the model is asked to check, the app saves the setup in force as the one checked. The model's own successful `printer_setup` fires nothing: the setup it chose is saved as checked at once (Kenneth, 2026-10-19), so the skill is for a setup that moved without the model, and a pairing its change breaks is caught by the slice-refusal facts and skill. It gives way to the file-loaded skill on a request that carries both, since that skill already asks for the same check.

+- `project-setup-changed` (trigger `setup_changed`): check the setup in force against the print's purpose. It fires on the result of an in-app `setup_record` that recorded a purpose for the first time or changed its fields (its result says which in `purposeChange`; a call that only restates the title to change the plan does not fire it), when the printer, filament, process or plate type differs from the setup the model was last asked to check under a recorded purpose (on the next tool result of the turn, or on the next turn's first request when the person changed it by hand), and on a turn's first request after the person restored an earlier version while a purpose is recorded. Each time the model is asked to check, the app saves the setup in force as the one checked. The model's own successful `printer_setup` fires nothing: the setup it chose is saved as checked at once (Kenneth, 2026-10-19), so the skill is for a setup that moved without the model, and a pairing its change breaks is caught by the slice-refusal facts and skill. It gives way to the file-loaded skill on a request that carries both, since that skill already asks for the same check.

- `slice-failed` (trigger `slice_failed`): a plate's last slice did not succeed, because OrcaSlicer's check refused the plate or the run failed. The adapter records why on the plate (`WorkspacePlate::slice_failure`: refused or failed, OrcaSlicer's words, the setting and object when named) at the moment it happens (a hook in `Plater::reslice`, `Workspace/SliceRequests.hpp`, and the run's completion event), worded by the print-issue monitor's `slice_failure_of`, and keeps it until the plate slices. Every request carries it as the plate's `sliceFailure`; `slice_report` of an unsliced plate adds the check code and the object's name. The skill fires once per failure, on the first request that carries it: the result of the model's own `slice_start`, the turn the app starts when a slice the model started fails after its turn, or the next message after the person's Slice all. The same refusal again is the same failure.

- `print-issues` (trigger `print_issues`): what the print-issue chip's two buttons ask for and how to read what OrcaSlicer reports. The adapter reads a slice's warnings through the monitor's `slice_warnings_of` while the plate is active and keeps a summary on the plate while that slice is current (`WorkspacePlate::slice_warnings`: the count, how many the person ignored, and the first warning, critical first, in OrcaSlicer's words with its setting and object). It counts every warning the chip lists, so the bed-temperature warning too, which `slice_report` leaves out. Every request carries it as the plate's `sliceWarnings`. The skill fires on the request that carries a chip's message, and on the first request whose workspace shows warnings no request has carried yet, whether the person sliced (their next message) or the model did (the tool result that shows them, or the app's turn when its slice ended after its turn); a re-slice with the same warnings fires nothing.

- `workspace_inspect` is offered through both adapters. Either side can then get the identity of a newly completed slice after slicing, without relying on the context it was given at the start of the turn.

- Import from an attachment (`object_import`) is in-app only, and import from a path (`object_import_file`) is MCP only. In the first case the file reaches the app through the conversation. In the second it arrives as an explicit path. These are two separate definitions that each say exactly what they do, both built on one workspace command. They are not one tool that behaves differently for different callers.

-- `intent_update` and `plan_set` are in-app only. The intent record and the pinned plan belong to the in-app chat. An external agent keeps what its user said, and its own plan, in its own conversation. MCP clients can still read both through `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report`. For the same reason, the in-app assistant's print guidance, which names these tools, is not part of the MCP server's instructions. That guidance is the "Intent and setup", "Preparation" and "Verification" paragraphs of the in-app prompt, written on the page in `AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`.

+- `setup_record` is in-app only. The intent record and the pinned plan belong to the in-app chat. An external agent keeps what its user said, and its own plan, in its own conversation. MCP clients can still read both through `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report`. For the same reason, the in-app assistant's print guidance, which names these tools, is not part of the MCP server's instructions. That guidance is the "Intent and setup", "Preparation" and "Verification" paragraphs of the in-app prompt, written on the page in `AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`.
- A future MCP diagnostics tool may be MCP only, if its purpose is to establish the external connection.

- The printer panel's five own tools carry only the `Printer` exposure. Neither adapter lists them. The panel's conversation offers all of them in every mode and refuses the calls that do not fit the conversation (see [Tool budget and tool shape](#tool-budget-and-tool-shape)). What the model reads back from one of these tools is the tool's own result. It is not wrapped in the host's workspace envelope.

Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>

    Record the reads Opus 5.5 sends, and tell intent_update to record only a stated purpose
    
    Squash of claude/opus-recorded-reads (24303e3a67, e7b7db2c69), re-recorded

    DeepSeek V4 Flash never sent, so the recording held no answer:

    - slice_report of a plate other than the active one.
    script.json's answers list now records slice_report for every plate by
    plateId and the changedOnly search for every object on every plate.
    recorded_answer in run_prompt_tests.py answers a changedOnly search from a
    recorded one with the same scope, target and query, whatever its limit, and
    never mixes searches with and without changedOnly. test_steps.py gains a test
    for each read; the changedOnly one fails with the old rule.

+         "Record the purpose the user stated as setupTitle, including when no setting changes. Never record one they have not stated, even marked assumed: ask them first. Send fields as an empty array for a title-only update. Project Undo does not undo this.",

judge, 3 each): print-this-no-purpose 1 passed, 2 failed (each asked two
questions where the case allows one; none recorded a guessed purpose);

call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's
  esbuild. This needs node and the AgentUI npm install. `--prompt-rev REV`
  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit
  that moved the prompt from C++ to the page, unchanged).
- **`project_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the project chat
  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:

  ```bash
  build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
      --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json tests/project_prompt/requests.json
  ```

  The harness runs the real app on its two-plate fixture (Bambu Lab X1 Carbon
  0.4, Bambu PLA Basic, 0.20mm Standard, plate 1 sliced) with the project
  chat's real OpenAI adapter, but the adapter's requests go nowhere: each is
  answered with the next model output the script gives. The tools run for
  real, and the app builds every request itself: the earlier turns as
  `AgentHost::make_agent_request` replays them (calls with their results, a
  result over 16 KiB replaced by the omission note, at most 20 entries), the
  new message as `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input` builds it (the
  person's words, then the app's `<print_issue>` and `<workspace>` blocks,
  each a part of its own), a canvas issue's message and context, a file-load report and its
  developer line, the file-loaded skill and the plate's picture on the
  request that first carries a load report, the print-issues skill on the
  request that carries a chip's message or first shows a slice's new
  warnings, the slice-failed skill on the request that first shows a
  refused or failed slice, the setup skill on the request that first
  carries a recorded or changed purpose or a setup change under one, and
  the live results of this turn's calls with the
  workspace block `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` adds. Arguments that need
  ids take them from the real previous result (`{{result/sessionId}}`) or the
  project (`{{workspace/activePlateId}}`). For each request it keeps, the
  harness checks the tools equal `project_tools.json` and the instructions
  equal `projectInstructions.fixture.txt`, then leaves both out of the file;
  the runner puts the rendered prompt and `project_tools.json` back. The
  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and
  answer against its tool's output schema.
- **Answered reads** are added as the app continues a turn: the model's own
  output items, then a result for every call under its call id, in the order
  the calls were written. Each answer carries the action id and workspace

content.content:
## Running it

By default every case runs 3 times (`RUN_BUDGET` 60 shared by the cases run,
at most 20 for one case alone); `--runs N` sets it. `--verbose` prints every
run's conversation. Usage is logged for every response on stderr and totalled
at the end.

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only --prompt-rev 6b4b8b6188 > bodies.jsonl
```

prints every request body it would send and their sizes, and sends nothing.

All runs of all the cases run share one pool of `--jobs` workers (5 by
default, 3 for the claude-cli backend below), and each run's line gives its
wall-clock time.

## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)

`--backend claude-cli` answers every step with the locally installed Claude
Code CLI in headless mode (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude
subscription instead of a per-token API key. `--judge claude-cli` moves the
judge there as well. Neither needs a key; both need the CLI logged in once
with `claude auth login`. The runner refuses to start a run the CLI would bill
to an API key (`apiKeySource` other than the login).

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --case advice-infill --runs 1
```

The model defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` at effort `medium`, both pinned so a
count moves only when the prompt does (`--claude-model`, `--claude-effort`,
`--claude-judge-model`). `--claude-keep DIR` keeps each run's session file,
tool list, MCP config and the CLI's event stream for reading afterwards.

### Which backend for what

- **Iterating on a prompt or skill: the subscription.** A strong model
  answering the app's real requests, with real tool calls, shows what the
  prompt itself causes: an ambiguous sentence, a rule two sections disagree
  on, a skill that invites the wrong call. It costs no API money, so it can
  be run as often as the subscription's usage limits allow. Those limits are
  shared with the developer's own Claude Code work; start with one case and
  keep `--jobs` small.
- **Before a release: a small paid run on the app's default model.** The app
  defaults to `gpt-5.4-mini` (the OpenAI provider's default in
  `ProviderProfile.hpp`), which scored about like DeepSeek V4 Flash in the
  printer suite's model table (82 and 79 of 87, `tests/printer_prompt`,
  "Which model"). A strong model
  can paper over an ambiguity a weaker one trips on, so a pass on Opus does
  not show the shipped default will pass. That run needs Kenneth's approval
  like every paid batch.
- **The baselines below** are DeepSeek V4 Flash with the OpenAI judge, except
  the subscription baseline, which is claude-cli's own. A claude-cli count is
  compared only with that one. Changing the judge changes
  what every judged case counts, so `--judge claude-cli` results start their
  own baseline, under the same "confirmed results become the baseline" rule.

### How a recorded request reaches the CLI

`claude_cli.py` turns each recorded request into a CLI run, and
`claude_mcp_stub.py` serves the tools:

- **System prompt**: the rendered prompt, as `--system-prompt`.
- **Tools**: the stub is a stdio MCP server with the case's tools (the 28 of
  `project_tools.json`, or the point's own list), with their real
  descriptions and schemas. Every call the model makes reaches the runner
  through it, and the step rules above apply unchanged: a read is answered
  with the recorded answer, a change ends the run (the runner stops the CLI;
  nothing is answered), a response of reads decides or is answered whole.
- **History**: the request's items before its last turn are written as a
  session file the CLI resumes (`--resume <file>`), so earlier messages,
  calls and results reach the model as its own turns, tool calls and tool
  results, not as a transcript. The last turn's message (the person's words,
  the `<workspace>` block, the plate's picture) goes in as one stream-json
  user message.
- **A point recorded mid-turn**, after a tool result (`after-preview`,
  `after-apply`, `after-slice`, `after-intent`, `direct-change-applied`,
  `direct-change-failed`, `first-person`, `slice-refused-by-tool`): the
  session ends on that turn's last call, marked as a deferred call. The CLI
  runs it through the stub, which returns the recorded result, and then asks
  the model.

Nothing from the developer's own Claude Code setup reaches the model: no
CLAUDE.md, auto-memory, settings, hooks, output style, skills, other MCP
servers or built-in tools, a minimal environment, and an empty temporary
working directory. `test_claude_cli.py` checks that, and the shapes above,
by running the installed CLI against a fake Messages endpoint on localhost
(no login, nothing sent; about 10 seconds). Run it after a CLI update: the
session file is the CLI's internal format, verified against 2.1.283.

What differs from the app's request, beyond the model:

- **Developer messages.** The Messages API has no developer role, so each of
  the app's developer items (its notes after a file-load report, the skills)
  is a user text block wrapped in `<developer_message>` tags. Hosts that
  drop or demote the developer role raise the same question for the API
  backend.
- **The CLI's own text.** Before the prompt, the CLI sends a billing header
  and "You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK."; after
  the first message it adds a short environment note (the temporary working
  directory, platform, date and model name) and an empty system turn
  carrying the effort setting.
- **Tool names** carry the CLI's MCP prefix: the model sees
  `mcp__jusprin__settings_get`, while descriptions, which name other tools
  bare, are unchanged. The runner strips the prefix.

## Running it

By default every case runs 3 times (`RUN_BUDGET` 60 shared by the cases run,
at most 20 for one case alone); `--runs N` sets it. `--verbose` prints every
run's conversation. Usage is logged for every response on stderr and totalled
at the end.

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only --prompt-rev 6b4b8b6188 > bodies.jsonl
```

prints every request body it would send and their sizes, and sends nothing.

All runs of all the cases run share one pool of `--jobs` workers (5 by
default, 3 for the claude-cli backend below), and each run's line gives its
wall-clock time.

## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)

`--backend claude-cli` answers every step with the locally installed Claude
Code CLI in headless mode (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude
subscription instead of a per-token API key. `--judge claude-cli` moves the
judge there as well. Neither needs a key; both need the CLI logged in once
with `claude auth login`. The runner refuses to start a run the CLI would bill
to an API key (`apiKeySource` other than the login).

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --case advice-infill --runs 1
```

The model defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` at effort `medium`, both pinned so a
count moves only when the prompt does (`--claude-model`, `--claude-effort`,
`--claude-judge-model`). `--claude-keep DIR` keeps each run's session file,
tool list, MCP config and the CLI's event stream for reading afterwards.

### Which backend for what

- **Iterating on a prompt or skill: the subscription.** A strong model
  answering the app's real requests, with real tool calls, shows what the
  prompt itself causes: an ambiguous sentence, a rule two sections disagree
  on, a skill that invites the wrong call. It costs no API money, so it can
  be run as often as the subscription's usage limits allow. Those limits are
  shared with the developer's own Claude Code work; start with one case and
  keep `--jobs` small.
- **Before a release: a small paid run on the app's default model.** The app
  defaults to `gpt-5.4-mini` (the OpenAI provider's default in
  `ProviderProfile.hpp`), which scored about like DeepSeek V4 Flash in the
  printer suite's model table (82 and 79 of 87, `tests/printer_prompt`,
  "Which model"). A strong model
  can paper over an ambiguity a weaker one trips on, so a pass on Opus does
  not show the shipped default will pass. That run needs Kenneth's approval
  like every paid batch.
- **The baselines below** are DeepSeek V4 Flash with the OpenAI judge, except
  the subscription baseline, which is claude-cli's own. A claude-cli count is
  compared only with that one. Changing the judge changes
  what every judged case counts, so `--judge claude-cli` results start their
  own baseline, under the same "confirmed results become the baseline" rule.

### How a recorded request reaches the CLI

`claude_cli.py` turns each recorded request into a CLI run, and
`claude_mcp_stub.py` serves the tools:

- **System prompt**: the rendered prompt, as `--system-prompt`.
- **Tools**: the stub is a stdio MCP server with the case's tools (the 28 of
  `project_tools.json`, or the point's own list), with their real
  descriptions and schemas. Every call the model makes reaches the runner
  through it, and the step rules above apply unchanged: a read is answered
  with the recorded answer, a change ends the run (the runner stops the CLI;
  nothing is answered), a response of reads decides or is answered whole.
- **History**: the request's items before its last turn are written as a
  session file the CLI resumes (`--resume <file>`), so earlier messages,
  calls and results reach the model as its own turns, tool calls and tool
  results, not as a transcript. The last turn's message (the person's words,
  the `<workspace>` block, the plate's picture) goes in as one stream-json
  user message.
- **A point recorded mid-turn**, after a tool result (`after-preview`,
  `after-apply`, `after-slice`, `after-intent`, `direct-change-applied`,
  `direct-change-failed`, `first-person`, `slice-refused-by-tool`): the
  session ends on that turn's last call, marked as a deferred call. The CLI
  runs it through the stub, which returns the recorded result, and then asks
  the model.

Nothing from the developer's own Claude Code setup reaches the model: no
CLAUDE.md, auto-memory, settings, hooks, output style, skills, other MCP
servers or built-in tools, a minimal environment, and an empty temporary
working directory. `test_claude_cli.py` checks that, and the shapes above,
by running the installed CLI against a fake Messages endpoint on localhost
(no login, nothing sent; about 10 seconds). Run it after a CLI update: the
session file is the CLI's internal format, verified against 2.1.283.

What differs from the app's request, beyond the model:

- **Developer messages.** The Messages API has no developer role, so each of
  the app's developer items (its notes after a file-load report, the skills)
  is a user text block wrapped in `<developer_message>` tags. Hosts that
  drop or demote the developer role raise the same question for the API
  backend.
- **The CLI's own text.** Before the prompt, the CLI sends a billing header
  and "You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK."; after
  the first message it adds a short environment note (the temporary working
  directory, platform, date and model name) and an empty system turn
  carrying the effort setting.
- **Tool names** carry the CLI's MCP prefix: the model sees
  `mcp__jusprin__settings_get`, while descriptions, which name other tools
  bare, are unchanged. The runner strips the prefix.
- **Mid-turn points**: after the deferred call's result, the CLI adds
  "Continue from where you left off." as a user message. The app's notes
  that follow the result there (the setup skill in `after-intent`, the
  slice-failed skill in `slice-refused-by-tool`) are further text blocks of
  that same tool result, since the CLI resumes no message after it.
- **Notes sent once** (a point's `once`) stay in the history after the
  first answered read; the app leaves them out of the turn's later requests.
- **Pictures** reach the model, unlike on the pinned DeepSeek hosts, so
  `model-opened-unnamed`, `model-imported-by-tool` and `model-opened-by-tool`
  can be measured here.

The usage the runner logs is the CLI's token count; on the subscription it is
not billed per token.

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### Sections for Test Organization
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Complex feature testing", "[Feature]") {
    // Common setup code
    SomeObject obj;
    
    SECTION("First scenario") {
        // Specific test case
        REQUIRE(obj.method1() == expected_value);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second scenario") {
        // Another test case with same setup
        REQUIRE(obj.method2() == other_expected);
    }
}
```

### BDD-Style Tests
Use for complex scenarios and user story testing:

> **Note**: BDD macros are aliases for TEST_CASE and SECTION with prefixed names
```cpp
SCENARIO("User performs complex operation", "[UserStory]") {
    GIVEN("A specific setup condition") {
        GCodeWriter writer;
        // Setup code
        
        WHEN("User performs action") {
            auto result = writer.some_operation();
            
            THEN("Expected outcome occurs") {
                REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
                
                AND_WHEN("Follow-up action occurs") {
                    auto next_result = writer.next_operation();
                    
                    THEN("Final outcome is correct") {
                        REQUIRE(next_result == expected);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Data Generators for Parameterized Tests
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Function works with various inputs", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto test_value = GENERATE(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13);
    
    REQUIRE(is_odd(test_value));
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Range-based generators
TEST_CASE("Range testing", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto i = GENERATE(range(1, 10));  // 1 to 9
    REQUIRE(process_value(i) > i);
}

// Using variables in generators (requires GENERATE_COPY or GENERATE_REF)
TEST_CASE("Generator with variables", "[Algorithm]") {
    std::vector<int> values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    auto test_value = GENERATE_REF(from_range(values));  // Use GENERATE_REF for references
    
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Custom generators
TEST_CASE("Random values", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto random_int = GENERATE(take(100, random(-1000, 1000)));  // 100 random values
    REQUIRE(process_random_value(random_int));
}
```

### Test Fixtures
```cpp
class GeometryFixture {
public:
    Point origin{0, 0};
    Point unit_x{1, 0};
    Point unit_y{0, 1};
    
    mutable double tolerance = EPSILON;  // Use mutable for data that might change
};

// Standard fixture - new instance per test run
TEST_CASE_METHOD(GeometryFixture, "Point operations", "[Geometry]") {
    REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
}

// Persistent fixture - single instance for entire test case (v3.2.0+)
TEST_CASE_PERSISTENT_FIXTURE(GeometryFixture, "Persistent operations", "[Geometry]") {
    static int call_count = 0;
    ++call_count;
    INFO("This fixture persists across sections, call: " << call_count);
    
    SECTION("First section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_y) == 1.0);
        // call_count will be 2 here with persistent fixture
    }
}

// Template fixtures for type-parameterized tests
template<typename T>
class NumericFixture {
public:
    T zero = T{0};
    T one = T{1};
};

TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE_METHOD(NumericFixture, "Numeric operations", "[Template]", int, float, double) {
    REQUIRE(TestType{} == this->zero);
    REQUIRE(TestType{1} == this->one);
}
```

### Advanced Testing Features

#### Logging and Information Macros
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Advanced logging", "[Logging]") {
    INFO("This info persists until end of scope");
    
    SECTION("Section A") {
        INFO("Section A specific info");
        CAPTURE(some_variable, another_var);  // Captures variable names and values
        CHECK(some_condition);
    }
    
    SECTION("Section B") {
        UNSCOPED_INFO("This survives beyond its scope");  // v2.7.0+
        CHECK(other_condition);
    }
}

// Warning and explicit control
TEST_CASE("Explicit test control", "[Control]") {
    WARN("This warns but doesn't fail the test");
    
    if (precondition_not_met) {
        SKIP("Reason");  // Marks the test as skipped (v3.3.0+, available)
        return;
    }
    
    if (critical_failure) {
        FAIL("Critical condition failed");  // Fails and stops test
    }
    
    SUCCEED("Reached successful completion");  // Explicit success marker
}
```

#### Static Assertions (Compile-time Testing)
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Compile-time checks", "[Static]") {
    STATIC_REQUIRE(sizeof(int) >= 4);  // Checked at compile time
    STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(std::is_void_v<int>);
    
    // For traits and template metaprogramming
    STATIC_CHECK(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<Point>);  // v3.0.1+
}
```

#### Conditional Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Conditional blocks", "[Conditional]") {
    int value = get_test_value();
    
    // These record the expression but don't count as test failures (v3.0.1+)
    CHECKED_IF(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value > 0
        REQUIRE(value <= 100);
    } CHECKED_ELSE(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value <= 0  
        REQUIRE(value >= -100);
    }
}
```

#### Benchmarking (v2.9.0+)
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance testing", "[Benchmark]") {
    // Simple benchmarking
    BENCHMARK("Algorithm performance") {
        return expensive_algorithm();
    };
    
    // Advanced benchmarking with setup
    BENCHMARK_ADVANCED("Advanced benchmark")(Catch::Benchmark::Chronometer meter) {
        std::vector<int> data = setup_test_data();  // Setup not measured
        
        meter.measure([&] { 
            return process_data(data);  // Only this is measured
        });
    };
}
```

## OrcaSlicer-Specific Testing Patterns

### Geometry Testing

```cpp
    // Large test data
```

### Custom String Conversions

#### For Custom Types
```cpp
// Method 1: operator<< overload (preferred)
std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Point& point) {
    os << "Point(" << point.x << ", " << point.y << ")";
    return os;
}

// Method 2: StringMaker specialization
namespace Catch {
```

## Running and Debugging Tests

### Building Tests
```bash
# Build all tests
cd build && make

# Build specific test suite
cd build && make libslic3r_tests

# Build and run tests
cd build && make && ctest
```

### Running Tests

#### Essential Test Execution Patterns
```bash
# REQUIRED: Random order with assertion warnings (best practice)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# Run all tests with verbose output via CTest
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure

# Run specific test suite with best practices
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# Filter tests with specific tags
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "[Geometry]" --order rand

# Filter by test name patterns
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "*geometry*" --order rand

# Exclude tests (negation)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "~[Performance]" --order rand

# Combine filters: (Geometry AND Config) OR Algorithm
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "[Geometry][Config],[Algorithm]" --order rand

# List available tests, tags, and reporters
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-tests
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-tags  
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-reporters

# Debug failing tests
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --break    # Break into debugger on failure
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --success  # Show passing tests too
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --durations yes  # Show timing info

# Abort on first failure
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --abort

# Test sharding for parallel execution (MUST share random seed)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 3 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
wait  # Wait for all to complete
```

#### Reporter Options for CI Integration
```bash
# Different output formats for CI systems
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter console     # Default human-readable
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter compact     # Minimal output
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter xml         # Catch2 XML format
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter junit       # JUnit XML (widely supported)

cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter automake    # Automake integration

# Multiple reporters simultaneously (if supported)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter console --reporter junit::out=results.xml
```

```cpp
using namespace Slic3r::Test;

// Load standard test meshes
TriangleMesh mesh = mesh(TestMesh::cube_20x20x20);

// Standard test configurations
DynamicPrintConfig config = config(TestConfig::PLA_default);
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

## Performance Considerations

### Compilation Optimizations
```cpp
// In CMakeLists.txt or as preprocessor definition
#define CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE  // 20% faster compilation, disables some features

// For faster test iteration during development
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION  // Workaround for VS2017 raw string bug
```

### Runtime Performance
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {
    // Manual timing example (Catch2's built-in BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto result = expensive_operation();
    
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.is_valid());
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
    
    INFO("Operation took " << duration.count() << "ms");
}
```

### Memory Leak Detection
```cpp
// For Windows builds - detects memory leaks
#define CATCH_CONFIG_WINDOWS_CRTDBG  // Must be defined for whole build
```

## Integration with CMake

### Adding New Test Files
1. Create test file: `test_new_feature.cpp`
2. Add to appropriate `CMakeLists.txt`:
```cmake
add_executable(${_TEST_NAME}_tests 
    ${_TEST_NAME}_tests.cpp
    test_existing_feature.cpp
    test_new_feature.cpp  # Add here
)
```

### Advanced Test Discovery
```cmake
# Basic test discovery
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: ")

# Advanced test discovery with customization
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: "
    TEST_SUFFIX " (auto)"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
    EXTRA_ARGS --order rand --warn NoAssertions
    PROPERTIES 
        TIMEOUT 300
        LABELS "unit;core"
    DISCOVERY_MODE PRE_TEST  # or POST_BUILD
    REPORTER junit
    OUTPUT_DIR ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/test-results
    OUTPUT_PREFIX "results_"
    OUTPUT_SUFFIX ".xml"
)

# Test sharding for parallel execution
include(CatchShardTests)  # If available
catch_shard_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    SHARD_COUNT 4
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}_shard: "
)
```

### Conditional Test Compilation
```cmake
# Feature-dependent tests
if (TARGET OpenVDB::openvdb)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_hollowing.cpp)
endif()

# Platform-specific tests
if(WIN32)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_windows_specific.cpp)
elseif(UNIX)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_unix_specific.cpp)
endif()

# Compiler-specific workarounds
if(MSVC)
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION)
endif()

# Fast compile mode for development
if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "Debug")
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE)
endif()
```

## Known Issues and Workarounds

### Platform-Specific Issues
```cpp
// MinGW/CygWin slow linking workaround
// Use: -fuse-ld=lld flag to speed up linking significantly

// Visual Studio 2017 raw string literal bug
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION
// This disables expression stringification but works around the compiler bug

// Visual Studio 2022 spaceship operator issue
// REQUIRE((a <=> b) == 0);  // May not compile with MSVC
// Workaround: use clang-cl or avoid spaceship in assertions

// QNX/VxWorks C stdlib issues
#include <cfoo>           // Use C++ headers
std::foo_function();     // Always call qualified
// NOT: #include <foo.h> and foo_function();
```

### Catch2 v3 Features Available
```cpp

// SKIP() macro                           - v3.3.0+
// Opt-in thread-safe assertions          - v3.9.0+ (NOT enabled here; see Thread Safety)
// Built-in BENCHMARK / BENCHMARK_ADVANCED - v3.x
// testCasePartial events                 - v3.0.1+
// Multiple reporters simultaneously      - v3.0.1+
// STATIC_CHECK macro                     - v3.0.1+
// Built-in test sharding (--shard-*)     - v3.x

// v3 notes to remember:
// - String matcher is "ContainsSubstring" (v2's "Contains" no longer exists)
// - Sections can still be re-run if a later section fails (unchanged from v2)
```

### Test Organization Best Practices

#### Project Structure Rules
1. **1:1 correspondence**: One test binary per library/module
2. **Hidden tests**: Use `[.]` or `[!benchmark]` tags for tests that shouldn't run by default
3. **Tag hierarchy**: Use consistent tagging scheme across the project
4. **File naming**: Follow `test_<feature>.cpp` pattern

#### CI/CD Integration
```bash
# Essential CI test command
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter junit::out=results.xml

# For coverage analysis
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter console --success

# For performance tracking
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --durations yes
```

This comprehensive guide ensures robust, maintainable, and efficient testing practices for OrcaSlicer development with Claude Code, incorporating all critical knowledge from the official Catch2 documentation.
