2026-10-20T15:36:06.311Z | Yes, there's been improvement on what you set out to fix, with two caveats: every result rests on 3 live runs, and merging the two tools introduced new failure modes. I fixed those as they appeared, but the last fix hasn't been tried live. One evaluation case also got worse, and I haven't explained it yet.

**Where we started (`jusprin-newui`, Oct 19):**
- **The setup card** showed up to two preset-difference rows, including formatting noise such as the thumbnail list, and no plan headline.
- **Intent and plan** were stored once for the project, and copied into each chat's checkpoint.
- **The plan went stale on the agent's own edits.** Of 381 recorded plan-validity values, 240 said `needs_reassessment`, caused by edits that carried out the plan.
- **Title and headline drifted apart when the goal changed.** In batch B, all three changed-strategy runs rewrote the headline, but only 1 of 3 updated the title. The card read "dried flowers, spiral vase" above "watertight multi-wall".
- **Titles described the setup, not the goal.** 7 of 12 batch-B titles named settings ("Rhino figurine — 0.16mm, 3 walls, organic supports").

**What I did (5 commits on `claude/setup-card-headline`, not pushed):**
1. **f964221268:** each chat owns its intent and plan, regions are saved with each model version, the schema is reset to 1 with no migration, and the card shows the headline instead of difference rows. The agent's own edits no longer mark the plan stale; the 240 stale values are now 0.
2. **28d6d67fdc:** `intent_update` and `plan_set` merged into `setup_record`, with the title required on every call.
3. **638abd5a41:** the title argument renamed to `purpose` (at most 60 characters, described as the person's goal, not how to print it).
4. **db65218fdc:** the plan flattened into top-level arguments, because DeepSeek sent the nested plan as a string and the app refused it.
5. **224e5ba135:** the plan's `assumptions` renamed to `unverified`, because DeepSeek put intent-field objects there.

**Live results on the changed-strategy journey (3 runs each, DeepSeek V4 Flash):**

| Batch | Code | Title follows the new goal | Titles goal-only | Refused calls that stopped a turn |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B | separate tools | 1 of 3 | no (settings in 2 of 3 titles) | 0 |
| C | merged tool, `setupTitle` | 2 of 3 (run 1 asked questions first) | no ("— 4 walls, 20% infill") | 0 |
| D | `purpose`, nested plan | 3 of 3 by the end (one needed a go-ahead turn) | yes | 2 runs, stringified plan |
| E | flat plan | 3 of 3 by the end (one needed a go-ahead turn) | yes | 1 run, empty `printer_setup_preview` (unrelated to this work) |

The last fix (the `unverified` rename) hasn't been run live. In batch E, 2 `setup_record` calls were refused and then succeeded on retry; that rename is meant to stop those.

**What improved:**
- **The card:** it shows the strategy instead of preset noise. This is checked end to end in the app, across all the card's states.
- **Storage:** intent and plan are stored once, on the chat. Resuming a chat or restoring a version keeps each chat's own records, and the regions come back with the model version.
- **Plan freshness:** the plan no longer goes stale on the agent's own edits.
- **Titles:** in batches D and E every title was goal-only ("Vase for fresh flowers in water", "Watertight vase for fresh flowers"), against 7 of 12 with settings in batch B.
- **Goal changes:** the title followed the new goal in 3 of 3 runs in each of the last two batches, against 1 of 3 at the start.

**What didn't improve, or got worse:**
- **Refused calls from the merge.** Each change to the tool's shape gave DeepSeek a new way to send a call the app refuses, and two refusals end a turn. Those cost real failures in batch D. The remaining fix is untested.
- **`answer-from-context` dropped** from 3/3 to 0/3 in the standard prompt evaluation (run on 638abd5a41). Asked which printer and filament the project uses, the model called `workspace_inspect` instead of ans
=====

1. **f964221268** — Store intent and plan on each chat; show the plan headline on the setup card (unchanged).
2. **6a2294b536** — Merge intent_update and plan_set into one tool, setup_record. The message describes the final shape and its reasons:
   - **Arguments:** `purpose` is required, at most 60 characters, and states the person's goal. `fields` is optional. The plan's `headline`, `decisions`, `unverified` and `risks` are flat and optional.
   - **Why:** a short paragraph explains each choice from the live runs.
   - **Not yet tested:** the message says that the last change, the `unverified` rename, hasn't been run live.
   - **Model input:** it lists every change to what the model sees.

The old hashes (28d6d67fdc, 638abd5a41, db65218fdc, 224e5ba135) are no longer on the branch. I've recorded the mapping in the shared notes folder.

Still open, both written down there:
- **`unverified` rename untested:** it hasn't been tried in a live run.
- **`answer-from-context` drop:** it fell from 3/3 to 0/3 in the Oct 19 evaluation, and I haven't explained it.
=====

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

Both setup-card commits are now on top of jusprin-newui in the main checkout, and everything passes. On Opus 5.5, the remaining DeepSeek failures mostly go away: `answer-from-context` passes 3 of 3. `print-this-no-purpose` is the exception; it fails on both models.

**The rebase.** `jusprin-newui` is now 5ca13e4234, then 334287e2d8 (per-chat intent and plan, setup card headline), then 2934817d87 (`setup_record`). Nothing is pushed. The old `claude/setup-card-headline` branch is untouched. Three things needed attention:
- `jusprin-newui` had moved the request-building code from `OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp` to `ProviderAgent.cpp`. I carried the `purpose` and `unverified` renames into the new file.
- `jusprin-newui` had added a rule to `intent_update`: never record a purpose the person hasn't stated, even marked as assumed. I carried it into `setup_record`'s description. Because `purpose` is now required on every call, this also means the model can't record a plan until the person has stated a purpose.
- Tests added on `jusprin-newui` still used `intent_update` and expected 28 tools. I updated them to `setup_record` and 27 tools.

**Checks, all passing:**
- 368 agent-bridge cases, 42 workspace-contract cases, 119 JusPrin cases and 446 page tests.
- Shell harness: default run (563 checks), chat restoration (68) and the setup-differences capture (118).
- Workspace harness: 6,004 checks.
- `project_tools.json` was regenerated and `requests.json` re-recorded. The removed names (`intent_update`, `plan_set`, `setupTitle`, `assumptions`, `origin`, `needs_reassessment`) no longer appear in either.

**Opus 5.5 on the subscription:** all 24 cases, 3 runs each, through the Claude CLI with the Claude judge. 70 passed, 2 failed, none unobserved. Today's subscription baseline on `jusprin-newui` was 69, 3 and 0. It used 1.9M input tokens (1.6M cached), all on the subscription.

| Issue from the DeepSeek run on the branch | DeepSeek | Opus 5.5 | My reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| `answer-from-context` (looks something up instead of answering from what it was given) | 0/3 | 3/3 | DeepSeek-specific |
| `reply-in-german` | 2/3, one reply in English | 3/3 | DeepSeek-specific |
| `print-this-no-purpose` (asks two questions where one is allowed) | 1/3 | 1/3 (baseline 0/3) | Not the model: the prompt or the case |
| Unobserved runs (reads the recording doesn't hold) | 6 | 0 | DeepSeek asks for reads nobody recorded |

Why I read `answer-from-context` as DeepSeek's problem:
- The message and workspace block DeepSeek saw are byte-for-byte the same as in its 3/3 baseline. Only two things changed: the tool list (two tools became `setup_record`) and one prompt line ("the print's purpose recorded with setup_record").
- Opus, given that same changed input, answered from context in all three runs.

Two limits on that reading:
- DeepSeek ran an earlier version of the tool (638abd5a41). Whether it still fails on the final version would need a paid DeepSeek run, which I didn't do.
- A pass on Opus doesn't prove the app's default model (`gpt-5.4-mini`) will pass. The test README makes the same point.

**Not committed yet.** Six files are uncommitted on top of 2934817d87: the regenerated tool list and recording, the 27-tool counts in three test files, and one README line. They belong in the `setup_record` commit, and folding them in means `git commit --amend` on 2934817d87. One more detail: the first commit, 334287e2d8, carries `jusprin-newui`'s recording rather than a re-recorded one. Re-recording it as well would need a second build, so I left it as it is.

content.content:
Merge intent_update and plan_set into one tool, setup_record

The setup card's title (what the person wants) and its headline (how the
agent will print it) were written by two tools, and the model kept them apart
badly: in batch B's changed-strategy journeys (2026-10-19) it rewrote the
headline with plan_set but never called intent_update, so the card read
"dried flowers, spiral vase" above "watertight multi-wall". The two records
were already handled as one (same coordinator block, both in-app only, both
on the chat, the same context push), so they are now one tool.

setup_record takes, all at the top level:
- purpose, required on every call, at most 60 characters: what the person
  wants the print to be or do, in a few words and their terms, not how to
  print it (no settings, material, printer or print mode unless the person
  made one of them the goal). It titles the setup card.
- fields, optional, with intent_update's semantics (assumed, question,
  provenance).
- headline, decisions, unverified, risks: the plan, optional. With a
  headline they replace the whole plan; with none the plan is kept, so a
  purpose can be recorded before there is a strategy. unverified is one
  sentence per thing taken as true without being able to check.
The result carries the intent section, purposeChange and the setup in force,
and always the plan as it now stands. The card's context is pushed once per
successful call, so title and headline arrive together.

The setup-changed skill fires on a first purpose or changed fields, as
before; a new purpose wording alone is title_only, and a call that only
restates the purpose to change the plan is unchanged, so neither fires it.

Why it looks like this (DeepSeek V4 Flash, live runs of 2026-10-19/20):
- "purpose", not "setupTitle": under either tool 7 of 12 batch-B titles,
  and some batch-C titles, described the setup ("Rhino figurine — 0.16mm,
  3 walls, organic supports"); with the rename and the description every
  title in two later batches was goal-only.
- A flat plan, not a nested object: the model sent the nested plan as a
  string of JSON, which the registry refuses; two refusals end a turn.
- "unverified", not "assumptions": next to fields' "assumed" flag, the
  model put intent-field objects under assumptions. This last rename has
  not been run live.

Changes to the model's input: one tool where there were two (27 project
tools), "purpose" and "unverified" in each turn's <workspace> block and in
tool results (including workspace_inspect's plan section), the project
prompt's line "the print's purpose recorded with setup_record, a setup that
suits it, checked, ...", and the setup-changed skill's "record the plan,
with what is unverified, using setup_record first".

tests/project_prompt: prepare-petg-strong also fails a setup_record whose
purpose says how to print (SETUP_WORDS); grading, script, README,
project_tools.json and requests.json updated and re-recorded with the
scripted model.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M5D006N0NQ4B6E6XF5ZZ3V67
